title: Sandiganbayan declares Zaldy Co’s 3 co-accused as fugitives
summary: The three are facing graft and malversation charges over alleged irregularities in the procurement and construction of a P289.4-million flood control project in Naujan, Oriental Mindoro

blocks.text: ANTI-GRAFT COURT. The Sandiganbayan in Quezon City.
The three are facing graft and malversation charges over alleged irregularities in the procurement and construction of a P289.4-million flood control project in Naujan, Oriental Mindoro
MANILA, Philippines – The Sandiganbayan Fifth Division has declared three co-accused of dismissed Ako Bicol representative Zaldy Co as fugitives.

In its ruling on Tuesday, November 10, the anti-graft court named Sunwest board members Anthony Ngo and Consuelo Aldon, and Department of Public Works and Highways Mimaropa materials engineer Timogen Sacar as fugitives. The court said they had demonstrated “an unmistakable intent to evade warrants and avoid prosecution.”

The three are facing graft and malversation charges over alleged irregularities in the procurement and construction of a P289.4-million flood control project in Naujan, Oriental Mindoro. The allegedly defective project was first exposed by Oriental Mindoro Governor Humerlito “Bonz” Dolor.

blocks.caption: Flood control anomalies: The case of Oriental Mindoro

blocks.text: According to prosecutors, the three remain at large despite the issuance of arrest warrants on November 21, 2025, nearly a year ago.

“Given the high-profile nature of the case, it is reasonable to conclude that the accused are aware of the criminal proceedings and the outstanding warrants issued against them. Thus, by staying beyond the reach of law enforcement while fully aware of pending warrants of arrest confirms accused’s deliberate intent to evade the judicial process,” the Sandiganbayan said.
Co, the beneficial owner of Sunwest, also remains at large despite facing multiple cases. He reportedly fled the country.
Sunwest was identified by President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. as one of the top flood control contractors under his administration.
The Sandiganbayan also ordered the cancellation of the passports of Ngo, Aldon, and Sacar to prevent them from seeking refuge overseas.

“Removing the official travel document necessary for the fugitive to leave the country or to travel between foreign countries hinders the attempts to evade judicial process,” the court said. – Rappler.com
